messages:
Alice Nguyen: Heads-up: spotted a reproducible throughput regression on multi-GPU runs when TP and PP are both enabled and using FP8/INT8 quantization. Overall throughput down ~18% vs baseline and NCCL allreduce times spike mid-step. Posting a short profiler slice below.

Ben Park: Can you paste the profiler output? my gut says nccl scheduling/backpressure or host-side pack/unpack stalls.

Alice Nguyen: profiler snippet (nvprof + nccl topo):
```
TIMELINE: step 120
GPU-util: 92% -> 18% drop at t=1.24s
NCCL allreduce: 1.24s - 1.40s (heavy)
CPU memcpy: 1.22s - 1.25s (blocking)
KV flush: triggered at 1.20s

nvprof:
GPU0  kernel conv_fwd     0.9ms
GPU0  pack_quant_gpu     15.3ms   <-- spike on pack
GPU0  ncclAllReduce      160.5ms
```

Carmen Li: Hmm that KV flush at 1.20s lining up with pack + nccl is suspicious. I've seen interleaved small allreduces starve compute when there are host-side packing phases. I have a tiny flame I generated earlier that looks similar (will paste excerpt):
```
|--- compute (150ms)
|   |--- forward kernels
|--- host pack (20ms)  <-- causes GPU to spinwait
|--- nccl allreduce (160ms)
|--- next compute delayed
```

Ryan O'Connor: Repro command I used locally:
`TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc_per_node=8 --nnodes=1 --node_rank=0 run_infer.py --tp-size 2 --pp-size 4 --quant-mode fp8 --batch 4`

Mira Patel: Two quick hypotheses: (1) KV cache flush is being scheduled on the host and overlaps badly with NCCL start/comms; (2) quant pack/unpack is currently CPU-bound for our tensor-parallel partition and gets serialized before nccl kickoff. Try disabling KV flush or moving pack to GPU. Also note PR #2345 added a batching heuristic that might change flush timing.

Alice Nguyen: I tried disabling KV writeback (set `--kv-flush=off`) — perf returned close to baseline. So KV flush + quant path seems to be the trigger. But why is it worse for FP8/INT8 vs FP16?

Ben Park: Because quant introduces extra packing/unpacking steps and often does a host->device memcpy for the packed buffer. That creates a host-side critical path: when the next NCCL kickoff waits for host-side completion you get a serialized pipeline. If pack is on CPU and we enqueue an nccl work that depends on that buffer, GPU sits idle waiting.

Carmen Li: Proposed immediate experiments:
- A: Defer KV flush until after allreduces for the step (cheap to prototype).
- B: Move pack/unpack to a fused GPU kernel (medium effort).
- C: Run with `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` and collect NCCL traces to confirm scheduling overlap.

Ryan O'Connor: I'll spin up a full 8xA100 job with the repro command and gather `nvprof` + `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` logs. ETA ~45m.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary build `gpu-runtime-1956` pushed to staging (sha:abc123). Tests: perf-smoke queued.

Mira Patel: Long-term we should: (1) add heuristics to delay KV flush when quant packing is active; (2) implement a GPU-pack kernel that writes already-packed tensors into NCCL buffers; (3) add an instrumentation probe for host memcpy times to our runtime tracing.

Ben Park: For (2) I'll sketch the GPU-pack kernel interface today: input FP32/FP16 tile -> quantize + pack -> write into NCCL buffer (pinned memory or GPU-buffer depending on path). That removes the extra memcpy/host dependency.

Carmen Li: I'll prototype (A) defer-flush patch and run microbenchmarks. If that fixes >90% of the regression we can ship a short-term mitigation.

Alice Nguyen: Action items: Carmen prototype defer-flush, Ben prototype GPU-pack interface, Ryan run full reproduce and upload traces, Mira coordinate PRs and perf verification. Sync at 16:00? :clock4:

Ryan O'Connor: SGTM, I'll drop logs in the thread when ready.

Alice Nguyen: Thanks all — this explains the weird mid-step throughput cliff. We'll follow up with traces + patch results in the thread. :thumbsup:
